text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Estonian-Scottish soccer game was abandoned after a protest from the Scots over poor floodlighting; the win was awarded to Scotland.
- The congress of Setu peoples, a small Finno-Ugric community, will appeal to international organisations over Russia's restricting their free movement in the indigenous Setu area.
- U.S. Defense Secretary William Perry said the Baltic countries were potential candidates for NATO and the press had misinterpreted his statement in Bergen.
- Rural parties say that the budget discussion in parliament will decide whether the ruling coalition stands or falls.
- Estonian members of the Estonia ferry commission were handed the report of the Swedish Maritime Department on divers operations. The newspaper reviews the report.

- Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi rejected the suspicions of the Moderates that two million kroons given to the Union of Agricultural Producers were to finance the election campaign of the Rural Parties Union.
- The investigation over the assassination attempt on the Ukrainian Prime Minister leads to the Donetsk clan and its contacts in Estonia.
- The government wants to upgrade the Estonian-Russian border talks, with either Foreign Minister Siim Kallas or Vaehi leading the Estonian team.
- The Justice Ministry is preparing amendments, establishing a 15 percent income tax on services, provided for offshore firms.
